claim: An LSTM deep-neural-network classifier running on cloud infrastructure fed by IoT sensor data over 5G achieved 97.13% accuracy in remotely classifying patient health status, a 10.41% average improvement over compared prior methods.
stance_target: cloud-based ML classification meaningfully improves accuracy of IoT remote patient monitoring over prior methods
scope_conditions: simulated in MATLAB across static (smart-home) and dynamic (mobile-health) scenarios
quoted_support: the accuracy of the proposed method is 97.13%, which has been improved by 10.41% in average over the other methods.

claim: Cloud computing combined with IoT sensor networks is positioned as a way to increase speed and accuracy of remote patient monitoring by offloading data storage, processing and classification off the edge device.
stance_target: architectural pattern of pairing a lightweight IoT sensing front end with cloud-side analytics
quoted_support: Using cloud computing and IoT in this process can significantly improve the monitoring of patients.
